english.title: Owner / master / operator make broadcast in prescribed areas of high seas causing interference in UK
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) you

(A)_[were the owner of a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..), which was not British-registered, while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas and from]_
(B)_[were the master of a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..), which was not British-registered, while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas and from]_
(C)_[were operating apparatus on a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..), which was not British-registered, while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas by means of]_
(D)_[participated in the operation of apparatus on a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..), which was not British-registered, while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas by means of]_

which a broadcast was made that caused interference with wireless telegraphy in the United Kingdom
english.legislation: Contrary to section 79(1)(b) and (2) and 93(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
owner of a ship not British-registered while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas
master of a ship which was not British-registered while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas OR
operated apparatus on a ship not British-registered while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas OR
participated in the operation of apparatus on a ship not British-registered OR
while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas
by means of which a broadcast was made
that caused interference with any wireless telegraphy in the UK

english.notes:
(i) Section 93(3) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that proceedings in England and Wales for this offence may be brought only by OFCOM or by or with the consent of the Secretary of State or the DPP.
(ii) Section 79(4) of the Act provides that the making of a broadcast does not contravene section 79(1) if it is shown to have been authorised under the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom.
(iii) Section 79(5) of the Act provides that prescribed means prescribed for the purposes of this section by an order made by the Secretary of State.
(iv) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(v) Section 94 of the Act provides a saving for broadcasts made under and in accordance with a wireless telegraphy licence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see paragraph 16 of Schedule 8 to the Act; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 35(2)(a) of the Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
